source_caption:
The Pursuit of Happyness isn’t about chasing a dream so much as refusing to let go of one.

Chris Gardner’s story doesn’t get softened for the screen. We see the nights in homeless shelters, the days spent trying to sell medical scanners nobody wants, and the weight of raising his son with nothing but stubbornness to work with.

There’s no big miracle moment here. It’s hundreds of small decisions to keep going when everything says stop. Will Smith carries that, but it’s the quiet stuff that sticks with you — shared meals, fake laughter to hide the fear, the tired walk back to the shelter at night.

The pursuit of happiness was never promised to be easy. But the film makes a strong case that just refusing to quit is its own kind of win.

source_details.synopsis: The Pursuit of Happyness is a 2006 American biographical drama film directed by Gabriele Muccino and starring Will Smith as Chris Gardner, a homeless salesman. Smith's son Jaden Smith co-stars, making his film debut as Gardner's son, Christopher Jr. The screenplay by Steven Conrad is based on the best-selling 2006 memoir of the same name written by Gardner with Quincy Troupe. It is based on Gardner's nearly one-year struggle being homeless. The intentional misspelling of the film's title comes from a mural that Gardner sees on the wall outside the daycare facility his son attended.
